properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 12 at 5:20PM MDT until August 12 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 520 PM MDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from 9
miles north of Westplains to 11 miles north of New Raymer, or along a
line from 31 miles northwest of Sterling to 33 miles west of
Sterling, moving east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Golf ball size hail and 70 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect
considerable tree damage. Wind damage is also likely to
mobile homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Westplains.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. These storms are capable of producing
widespread damaging winds and dangerous hail.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and

Wildcat Creek near Jerome.

.Radar estimates of 2 to 6 inches of rainfall within the past 24

forecast.

this portion of Wildcat Creek. Only two floods since 1961...July
2003 and April 2013...crested above this level. Flood affects most
roads near Wildcat Creek and the canoe launch near SR 213.

- At 6:15 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 12.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 6:15 PM EDT Wednesday was 12.3 feet.

feet just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below
flood stage late tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

AM EDT.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Indianapolis IN has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Indiana...

Flatrock River at Saint Paul.

.Radar estimates of up to nearly 7 inches of rainfall in eastern
Shelby County in the past 24 hours is quickly bringing flooding to
the Flatrock River at Saint Paul.  The river level is expected to
rise well above flood stage of 6 feet and possibly reach moderate
flood stage of 10 feet tonight.

On the positive side, remaining forecast rainfall over the next
couple days should be less than half an inch.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Flatrock River at Saint Paul.

* WHEN...From this evening to early Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Significant flooding in progress along the
Flatrock River.  Local river roads are flooded with possibly a few
residential areas affected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:45 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 6.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 5:45 PM EDT Wednesday was 6.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.7
feet late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage late
tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement should be issued Thursday morning by around 930
AM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 12 at 1:13PM AKDT until August 14 at 4:30AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Mendenhall Lake gauge levels, along with USGS imagery from Suicide
Basin and water levels within the basin, indicate that the basin is
continuing its release of water into Mendenhall Lake and River.
Levels on the Mendenhall Lake and River will rise through today as
the release continues, with a forecast crest between 16.1 to 16.6
feet expected Thursday morning.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst is
expected.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Drive and below Back Loop bridge.

* WHEN...Until 430 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the area around Mendenhall Lake and along the
Mendenhall River is imminent. Water levels will continue to rise
through today while water temperatures will fall within the lake
and river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 845 AM AKDT, gauge data reported a glacier-dammed lake
outburst is ongoing. Flooding is expected to begin shortly near
the Mendenhall Lake And River.
- The outburst flood forecast is based on an estimated volume of
water in the glacier dammed lake and an estimated release rate
based on previous events. The extent of water drainage within the
basin (partial or full) can vary widely between outburst flood
events and is a major source of uncertainty in the forecast,
particularly with regard to the peak flood stage.
- For Mendenhall Lake :
At 12:30pm the stage was 6.36 feet and rising.
Flood Stage is 9 feet.
Forecast: A crest between 16.1 and 16.6 feet is expected around
8am and noon Thursday. Water levels will go above minor flood
state around 9:30pm Wednesday. Water levels will go above major
flood stage around 5:45am Thursday.

Impacts:
At 6.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the "causeway"
at the end of the trail.

At 7.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the beginning of
the trail. Along the Mendenhall River some sections will experience
bank erosion resulting in dangerous tree fall. These conditions could
make floating the river more hazardous with the higher water levels.

At 9 feet: Water starts to cover Skaters Cabin Road between Skaters
Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead, also water will flow into the
Mendenhall Lake Campground.

At 10 feet: Water levels will inundate Mendenhall Campground with up
to 3 feet of water covering low areas as well as up to 1.5 feet of
water covering Skaters Cabin Road. Portions of West Glacier Trail
will be impassable. Areas along View Dr will start to flood and cause
minor flooding of yards. Closure of pedestrian pathways beneath
Brotherhood Bridge and the trail system on the west side of
Mendenhall River during outburst events.

At 11 feet: Some homes along View Dr will have up to 1.5 feet of
water in yards. Locations below back loop bridge will see bank
erosion along unreinforced river banks along with hazardous
navigation from debris in the river. Homes along the river on Meander
Way will begin to see flooding of some backyards on the outside of
the HESCO levee. Portions of the Dredge Lake Trail System will be
impassable. Flood waters start to reach Dredge Lake.

At 12 feet: Significant bank erosion along unreinforced river banks.
The low section of road past 9374 View Dr will be flooded with up to
0.5 feet of water. Some houses on the south side and the east end of
View Dr will start to flood. Water begins to flood some backyards of
homes on the northside of View Dr as well as other low lying areas.
Back Loop Rd Bridge will be closed during outburst events.

At 13 feet: The low section of road past 9374 View Dr will be flooded
with 2 ft of water. Water begins to flow through some backyards of
homes on the northside of View Dr and flood low lying areas. A few
locations on View Dr will see depths of 1 to 2 feet of water in
homes.

At 14 feet: The low section of road past 9374 View Dr will be
significantly flooded and impassable. Water will begin to flow over
the road from water flowing behind homes on the north side of View
Dr. More homes along View Dr will begin to see moderate to major
flooding. Locations on River Rd with low river banks will begin to
see water approach driveways.

At 15 feet: Major flooding of multiple homes along View Dr. Water
will begin to approach a few homes along River Rd with low river
banks with possible flooding of driveways and 1 to 2 feet of water in
backyards. Up to 1 foot of water covering Riverside Dr at Tournure St
and Mendenhall River School.

At 16 feet: Water starts to overtop the bank and flood low lying
areas near Wildmeadow Ln. Up to 0.5 feet of water will be in the
intersection of Skaters Cabin Rd and Arctic Cir. Some backyards of
homes between Tamarack Ct and Whitewater Ct will start to see flood
waters along with water approaching River Rd near homes with low
river banks and possibly flooding those homes. Water will start to
flood backyards of homes on Meadow Ln and Stikine St.

At 17 feet: This is an estimate that water will be overtopping the
river banks and flooding into the homes around Wildmeadow Ln.
Businesses in the Vintage Park Blvd area will be surrounded and
potentially inundated by flood waters. Homes on Meadow Ln from
Stikine St to Eagle St will be inundated with flood water. Water will
be covering Tournure St from Riverside Dr to Columbia Blvd. Black
Wolf Way and Pond Vista Dr will have water across the roads. All
parts of View Dr will be covered by flood water.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

The cold water temperatures can increase the threat of hypothermia
and lower the time required to cause hypothermia.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 12 at 1:50PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology, Benton Clean Air Agency,
and the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency have issued an Air Quality
Alert until further notice.

An Air Quality Alert has bee issued for Benton, Columbia, Franklin,
Kittitas, Walla Walla, and Yakima Counties until further notice due
to expected wildfire smoke from regional fires. North to northeast
winds will push smoke into the Columbia Basin beginning Wednesday
afternoon. Particulate matter (PM2.5) levels may reach Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups or worse. While occasional clearing and intermittent
good air quality is possible during periods of stronger winds, smoke
production continues to be significant from regional fires. Be sure
to check air monitors in your area before outdoor activities. When
air quality is Unhealthy, everyone should reduce exposure. Limit time
outside, avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and follow tips for
cleaner indoor air.


Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.
Information from the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.yakimacleanair.org or call 509-834-2050.
Information from the Benton County Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.bentoncleanair.org or call 509-783-1304.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 12 at 1:50PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air Quality
Advisory until at least 3 PM PDT Friday.

DEQ expects the air quality advisory to last until at least Friday
afternoon, August 14, 2026. DEQ and partner agencies will continue to
monitor smoke.

Smoke levels can change rapidly depending on weather. Check current
conditions on the Oregon Smoke Information Blog, DEQ's Air Quality
Index, or by downloading the free OregonAIR app on your smartphone.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

For additional information...please visit the Web site at
http://www.oregon.gov/DEQ

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Indianapolis IN has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Indiana...

Big Blue River at Carthage.

Clifty Creek at Hartsville.

.Copious rainfall in the past 24 hours, totaling as much as 5 inches
in Bartholomew County and 8 inches in Rush County, are quickly
bringing flooding to the Big Blue River and Clifty Creek today.
Rainfall will taper off the rest of the day, with additional amounts
expected to be under four tenths of an inch.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Blue River at Carthage.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, Extensive flooding is in progress. Many
local roads flood and are impassable to most vehicles. A few
evacuations are necessary in southern parts of Carthage, extreme
southern sections of Knightstown, eastern Raysville and a few
rural areas of northwest Rush County. Used auto parts yard in
Carthage is flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 6.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.1
feet late tonight.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement should be issued Thursday morning by around 700
AM EDT.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued August 12 at 12:16PM PDT until August 13 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Fire Weather
Watch for lightning and gusty outflow winds, which is in effect
from Thursday morning through Thursday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 652 West Portion of the
Olympic Mountains, Fire Weather Zone 658 West Slopes of the
North Cascades Generally above 1500 Feet and Fire Weather Zone
661 East Portion of the Olympic Mountains.

* LIGHTNING...Isolated to scattered thunderstorm coverage is
possible across the northern Cascade Mountains and the Olympic
Mountains. Thunderstorms will develop today from the northwest
and spread across the area.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Any storms that develop will be capable of
gusty and erratic outflow winds between 20 and 30 miles per
hour. Outflow winds can occur ahead of and behind storms and
cause erratic wind directions.

* IMPACTS...Scattered lightning in dry fuels can cause multiple
fire starts. Thunderstorms can also bring sudden sharp wind
shifts on existing fires, causing rapid changes in a fire's
rate of spread and direction of spread. Thunderstorm outflow
winds can be a threat for several hours following the start of
a new lightning-caused fire. If a fire were to begin, air
quality may diminish in the surrounding area.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either imminent or occurring now. Any fires that develop will
likely spread quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

A Fire Weather Watch means that there is a potential for critical
fire weather conditions to develop. Monitor the forecasts for
possible Red Flag Warnings.

Environmental Protection Agency

...AIR QUALITY ADVISORY FROM THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to

* IMPACTS...Members of sensitive groups may experience health

quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

Douglas, Ferry, Garfield, Grant, Lincoln, Okanogan, Pend Oreille,
Spokane, Stevens, and Whitman Counties until further notice due to

outdoor activities.

for cleaner indoor air.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 12 at 11:56AM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the following agencies:

Washington Department of Ecology
Colville Confederated Tribes
Environmental Protection Agency
Spokane Regional Clean Air Agency

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Adams, Asotin, Chelan,
Douglas, Ferry, Garfield, Grant, Lincoln, Okanogan, Pend Oreille,
Spokane, Stevens, and Whitman Counties until further notice due to
current and expected smoke from regional fires. Particulate matter
(PM2.5) may reach Unhealthy levels for areas directly downwind from
active wildfires. Other areas may reach Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups or worse. While occasional clearing is possible during periods
of stronger winds, smoke production continues to be significant from
regional fires. Be sure to check air monitors in your area before
outdoor activities.

Limit time outside, avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and follow tips
for cleaner indoor air.

properties.areaDesc: Bonner, ID; Boundary, ID
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 12 at 11:56AM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Advisory has been issued by the following agencies:

Idaho Department of Environmental Quality in Coeur d'Alene
Environmental Protection Agency

...AIR QUALITY ADVISORY FROM THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY FOR Boundary, Bonner, Counties...

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke. Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...Boundary, Bonner Counties...

* WHEN...Next update 12 PM August 14th.

* IMPACTS...Members of sensitive groups may experience health
effects.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

THIS STATEMENT IS ISSUED BY THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY, AIR QUALITY GROUP FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT DEQ's
Coeur d'Alene Regional Office at (208) 769-1422
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Kent; Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches; Cumberland; Cape May; Atlantic Coastal Cape May
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued August 12 at 2:51PM EDT until August 13 at 1:00AM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...In Delaware, Kent, Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.
In New Jersey, Cumberland, Cape May and Atlantic Coastal Cape
May.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 1 AM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated tides due to the New Moon today
may lead to minor coastal flooding during the evening high tides
through Thursday.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 7 PM THIS EVENING TO 1 AM EDT THURSDAY

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 12 at 12:49PM MDT until August 12 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of western New Mexico.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms will develop over the area today then
move slowly northward across western NM through tonight. Rainfall
rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour will occur with the heavier
storms. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall are possible in some
areas.
- This includes the Chuska mountains, Gallup, Zuni Pueblo, and
areas near the Sacaton wildfire burn scar in Catron county.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood

properties.areaDesc: Carroll, IN; Howard, IN
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 12 at 2:42PM EDT until August 13 at 12:51PM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Indianapolis IN has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Indiana...

Wildcat Creek at Kokomo.

.Radar estimates of 2 to 6 inches of rainfall in Howard County
within the past 24 hours, ending at 2 PM EDT today, along with
ongoing rain is bringing flooding to much of central Indiana along
and east of I-65.  Flooding is expected to develop on the Wildcat by
late-afternoon today.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wildcat Creek at Kokomo.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to early tomorrow afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 16.8 feet, In late December 1990, 60 homes flooded in
the Kokomo area. The Hillcrest area had one to three feet of water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 9.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 16.5
feet late this evening. It will then fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement should be issued late tonight by around 545 AM
EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM THIS AFTERNOON TO EARLY TOMORROW AFTERNOON

properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued August 12 at 12:42PM MDT until August 14 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Great Falls MT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
are possible over the Horse Gulch burn scar.

* WHERE...A portion of central Montana, including the following
areas, Horse Gulch burn scar, including Riverside Campground.

* WHEN...Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Horse Gulch burn scar is expected
up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near the Horse
Gulch burn scar should prepare for potential debris flow. Be sure
to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy
rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, urbanized
street flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Horse Gulch burn scar, which may lead to flash
flooding and debris flows. Additional heavy rainfall is possible
on Friday, and additional flood statements may be needed over the
coming days.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Horse Gulch burn scar and Riverside Campground.
- For flood safety, go to this web page.
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of

pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances. Take extra precautions if you work or spend time
outside. When possible reschedule strenuous activities to early

calling the United Way of Greater Saint Louis at 800-427-4626, or if
calling from a land line phone dial 2-1-1. You can also call Cool
Down Saint Louis at 314-241-7668.

* WHERE...Harney and Malheur Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL NOON PDT FRIDAY.

* IMPACTS...Smoke can irritate the eyes, lungs and worsen some
medical conditions. People most at risk to adverse health effects
include infants, young children, people with heart or lung
disease, older adults, and pregnant women.

weather. Check current conditions on the Oregon Smoke Information
Blog, DEQ's Air Quality Index, or by downloading the free
OregonAIR app on your smartphone.
properties.instruction:

* Avoid strenuous outdoor activity.

* Use high efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters in indoor
ventilation systems or portable air purifiers.

* Be aware of smoke in your area and avoid places with the highest
levels.

* If you have heart or lung disease, or asthma, follow your
healthcare provider's advice.

https://www.oregon.gov/deq

problems. Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 12 at 11:29AM EDT until August 13 at 2:37AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...

Tippecanoe River at Oakdale Dam at Lake Freeman near Yeoman.

Tippecanoe River near Delphi.

Wabash River at Lafayette.

.Heavy rainfall across northern and central Indiana will make its
way into the Tippecanoe and Wabash Rivers and bring minor lowland
flooding along those rivers. Additional rainfall amounts of 1.5 to
2.5 inches through Friday morning in the upper parts of those basins
was included in the forecast, so any deviations from that could
change the crests and amount of time in flood.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Tippecanoe River at Oakdale Dam at Lake Freeman near
Yeoman.

* WHEN...Until just after midnight tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 13,000.0 cfs, Extensive lowland flooding with flows
between 13,000 and 18,000 cubic feet per second.  Water at
dangerous levels with a few evacuations and minimal property
damage.  Some local river roads begin to flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM EDT Wednesday the flow was 10,500.0 cfs.
- Forecast...The flow is expected to increase above flood stage
this afternoon to a maximum of 13,200.0 cfs this afternoon.
- Flood flow is 13,000.0 cfs.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive
cars through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement should be issued this evening by around 1000 PM
EDT.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 12 at 8:15AM MDT by NWS Great Falls MT
properties.description:
AQAMT

The Montana Department of Environmental Quality has issued an air
quality alert for Beaverhead, Deer Lodge, Granite, Silver Bow,
Madison, Missoula, Ravalli counties in effect until 9AM on 08/13/2026
An Air Quality Alert means that particulates have been trending
upwards and that an exceedance of the 24 hour National Ambient Air
Quality Standard (NAAQS) has occurred or may occur in the near
future.

Elevated particulate levels from wildfire smoke

As of 8AM on 08/12/2026, particulate levels in Dillon are Unhealthy.

As of 8AM on 08/12/2026, particulate levels in Frenchtown and
Missoula are Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

As of 8AM on 08/12/2026, particulate levels in Billings, Butte,
Choteau, Columbia Falls, Cut Bank, Great Falls, Hamilton, Havre,
Helena, Lewistown, Libby, Malta, Sleeping Giant, Thompson Falls and
West Yellowstone are Moderate.

When air quality is Unhealthy... State and local health officials
recommend that people with respiratory or heart disease, the elderly,
and children should avoid prolonged exertion; everyone else should
limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups... State and local
health officials recommend that people with respiratory or heart
disease, the elderly and children should limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Moderate... State and local health officials
recommend that unusually sensitive people should consider reducing
prolonged or heavy exertion.

For more information visit the Montana Department of Environmental
Quality at http://todaysair.mtdeq.us
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

Pine. In north central Nevada, Southern Lander and Southern
Eureka. In south central Nevada, Northeastern Nye and Northwestern
Nye.

burn scars.

to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 12 at 1:11AM MST until August 13 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Elevated potential for Flash Flooding due to excessive
rainfall.

* WHERE...Yavapai County, Coconino County, Navajo County, Apache
County and northern Gila County.

* WHEN...From Noon MST Wednesday through Midnight MST Wednesday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- High moisture values and increased instability will lead to
strong thunderstorms today and this evening.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

Consider changing your plans if you were going to hike, boat, or
paddleboard to a slot canyon or normally dry wash. If you do still
decide to recreate, check in at a nearby visitor center or ranger
station.

properties.areaDesc: Benton, WA; Columbia, WA; Franklin, WA; Kittitas, WA; Walla Walla, WA; Yakima, WA
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 12 at 12:47AM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology, Benton Clean Air Agency,
and the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency have issued an Air Quality
Alert until further notice.

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Benton, Columbia, Franklin,
Kittitas, Walla Walla and Yakima counties until further notice due
to expected wildfire smoke from regional fires. Expect some clearing
out and intermittent good air quality but with significant fires on
the landscape conditions can worsen quickly to unhealthy air. Be sure
to check air monitors in your area before outdoor activities.

People can take the following precautions to protect their health:

* Follow local burn restrictions to prevent deteriorating air
quality.
* Avoid strenuous outdoor activity in smoky conditions.
* People with heart or lung problems and young children are
especially vulnerable. These people should stay indoors while
smoke levels are high.
* Use certified High Efficiency Particulate Air (HEPA) filters in
indoor heating ventilation, cooling, and air purification systems.
* Avoid using wood-burning stoves and other sources of indoor smoke
if possible.

Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.
Information from the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.yakimacleanair.org or call 509-834-2050.
Information from the Benton County Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.bentoncleanair.org or call 509-783-1304.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 12 at 12:47AM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air Quality
Advisory until noon PDT today.

For the Smoke Air Quality Advisory, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

For additional information...please visit the Web site at
http://www.oregon.gov/DEQ
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 12 at 3:15AM EDT until August 12 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 108 to 112 expected.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances. Take extra precautions if you work or spend time
outside. When possible reschedule strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion
and heat stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when
possible. To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety
and Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks
in shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued August 12 at 12:43AM MDT until August 14 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
are possible over the Big Rock burn scar.

* WHERE...The Big Rock burn scar near Heise.

* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Big Rock burn scar is possible
Thursday afternoon into Thursday evening. Anyone in or near the Big
Rock burn scar should prepare for potential debris flow moving
through the Big Rock burn scar. Be sure to stay up to date with
information from local authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger
flash flooding and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall near the Big Rock burn scar, which may lead to flash
flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Heise.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued August 11 at 11:14PM PDT until August 13 at 2:00AM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.4 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 2 AM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.4 ft above normal (7.24 ft MLLW) at 11:49
PM Wednesday 8/12. These predictions include both astronomical
tides and roughly 3-6 inches of additional water mainly from a
combination of thermal expansion and accumulated sea level rise
since the tidal datum was established (1983- 2001). High tide
varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast
and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 11 at 2:42PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
The warmest stretch of weather so far this summer is expected from
Wednesday through the weekend. High temperatures warming into the
upper 70s or lower 80s each day with lows dipping into the 50s are
expected. Areas of wildfire smoke across the middle Tanana Valley
are already reducing air quality. Light winds are unlikely to
clear out the smoke.

Drinking plenty of fluids, avoiding strenuous outdoor activity,
and limiting exposure to smoke is recommended.

properties.description: The Extreme Heat Watch has been replaced. Please see the latest information from NWS Springfield MO on this developing situation.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WARNING IN EFFECT FROM NOON TODAY TO 8 PM CDT WEDNESDAY
